title: Hybrid quant lab heuristics demo - HelixHealth
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console focused on hybrid quantization heuristics (INT8 / FP8) using HelixHealth's clinical QA prompt set. Demo included live benchmark results, caveats for EHR domain hallucination risk, and private deployment considerations (VPC, KMS). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with targeted quality thresholds and an A/B canary in staging.
topics: quality measurement and eval sets for EHR
private deployment constraints: VPC, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Rajiv Nair: yes, loud and clear. thanks Maya.
[00:12] Ethan Brooks: great, i'll share my screen and we'll jump into the Optimize console — apologies if there's a slight lag.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: screen's good. curious to see the int8/fp8 numbers on our clinical prompts.
[00:28] Maya Chen: perfect. quick intro — i'm maya (AE) and ethan is our se. you're all on the notes? we've got the helixhealth eval set preloaded per the doc you uploaded.
[00:40] Markus Vogel: yes, we dropped the sample batch yesterday — 1.2k prompts, mixture of discharge summaries and med history Qs.
[00:48] Ethan Brooks: awesome, so what i'll do is show three profiles: default fp16, int8 aggressive, and a hybrid-rule-based fp8 profile. we'll run latency and qa-quality side-by-side.
[00:58] [01:15] Ethan Brooks: starting with the baseline — fp16 on rdx-gpu-8 (our standard hosted GPU). p50 token latency is ~22ms, p95 about 78ms for the 512-token window with kv cache warm. accuracy baseline on your QA exact-match is 89.7%.
[01:35] Lena Ortiz: that's consistent with our earlier runs. what's the tokenization difference? we're using clinical tokenization?
[01:42] Ethan Brooks: yes, same tokenizer you used. there are some small mismatches occasionally — transcription flagged a couple model names as 'redwood-infer' — ignore that.
[01:50] [02:10] Ethan Brooks: switching to int8 aggressive profile. note we lowered quant thresholds and disabled per-layer fallback. p50 drops to 14ms, p95 to 52ms. throughput jumps by ~1.6x. quality delta: exact-match down to 87.9% (a -1.8pt absolute). we see some formatting regressions on tabular med lists.
[02:35] Rajiv Nair: formatting regressions are painful for downstream parsers. how big are hallucinations? any risk of inventing medications?
[02:45] Ethan Brooks: great question — hallucination rate (as measured by our hallucination detector) increased from 0.6% to 1.4% for int8 aggressive. a majority are subtle attribute swaps, rare drug invention but we flagged a few false positives during named-entity extraction.
[03:05] [03:30] Ethan Brooks: now hybrid fp8 profile — what we call heuristic hybrid: keep critical attention layers in fp16, quantize feed-forward to fp8, and enable per-request prefix caching. p50 sits at 16ms, p95 at 60ms. quality is 89.0% — so only a 0.7pt drop from baseline but with ~1.35x throughput.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: interesting — so hybrid fp8 seems like a middle-ground. how deterministic are those heuristics across different prompt lengths?
[04:05] Ethan Brooks: for short prompts (<128 tokens) the delta is smaller; for long generation cases (>512 tokens) we see fp8 sensitivity mainly in rare factual chains. our console includes per-prompt sensitivity scores so you can identify which prompt families to exclude from aggressive profiles.
[04:30] [04:55] Maya Chen: to add — Optimize will synthesize a "sensitivity cohort" that groups prompts by failure mode; you can review and decide which to pin to safer profiles.
[05:05] Markus Vogel: what's the deployment path for these profiles — hosted vs dedicated vs private? we need VPC for PHI.
[05:12] Ethan Brooks: with private (VPC) deployments we give the same console surface. the difference is model kernels and quant binaries are shipped in the private runtime; we support HSM/KMS integration for keys and full audit logs. latency numbers in private on customer infra will vary; we recommend a small dry-run in your staging GPUs to calibrate.
[05:35] [05:55] Rajiv Nair: and SOC 2 reports? our security team will ask for encryption at rest and in transit plus audit trail.
[06:02] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs — i'll share the package after the call. we also support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.
[06:15] [06:35] Ethan Brooks: back to the console — here's the per-prompt diff view. you can see one patient discharge prompt where int8 stripped a colon and collapsed a med dose field, causing downstream parser mismatch. we annotate the diff and give a suggested rule: keep that prompt family on fp16 or hybrid fp8 with layer 5 fallback.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: can we automate rules? we'd prefer not to manually curate hundreds of prompts.
[07:05] Ethan Brooks: yes — Optimize has an auto-suggest policy engine. it will propose a policy that maps prompt cohorts to quant profiles; you can accept or tweak before rollout. it can also create a canary rollout with traffic percentages and automatic rollback if eval metrics drop below threshold.
[07:30] [07:50] Rajiv Nair: demo the canary please.
[07:52] Ethan Brooks: sure — starting a 10% canary: profile applied, routing policy set to prefer low-latency for non-critical endpoints, and fallback to baseline on regression. initiating now... (console action) ...canary started. initial live p50 for canary requests matches the offline bench roughly.
[08:20] Lena Ortiz: how do we tie this to our test harness? we run nightly regression tests.
[08:28] Ethan Brooks: you can plug your harness into our eval API. we support ingesting your CSV of test prompts and will return per-prompt metrics including exact-match, F1, hallucination score, and latency. that's what we did with your 1.2k set earlier.
[08:50] [09:10] Maya Chen: quick note on billing: the cost model for hybrid profiles is token-based with adjustments for quantization compute delta. we'll include a sample cost projection for your 100k monthly tokens.
[09:25] Markus Vogel: so if we run the pilot in staging for 2 weeks, what's the min commitment?
[09:31] Maya Chen: for hosted pilot, no long term commit — pay-for-usage. for private, we typically do a short reserved window for container images; i'll put the minimal pilot options in the pricing email.
[09:45] [10:05] Rajiv Nair: can we request specific kernel builds? we have older A100 nodes and a mix of H100s.
[10:12] Ethan Brooks: yes — Optimize will recommend a kernel per hardware profile. for A100 we often prefer certain matmul kernels; for H100 fp8 has better stability on newer kernels. we can schedule a kernel-compatibility bench on your hardware — takes ~48 hours to run.
[10:32] Lena Ortiz: any concerns about label drift? clinical language changes a lot.
[10:38] Ethan Brooks: that's where continuous eval helps — we can set alerts for quality regressions per cohort and trigger re-eval automations or rollbacks.
[10:50] [11:15] Maya Chen: quick Qs from your side?
[11:20] Markus Vogel: deployment logistics: image signing and SBOM?
[11:26] Maya Chen: yes we support signed images and provide SBOMs for the runtime. also audit log streams can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog or cloud-native connectors.
[11:40] Rajiv Nair: good. can we see an export of the per-prompt diffs?
[11:45] Ethan Brooks: i'll export and share — linking the artifact in notes (link: drive/helix_quant_diffs.xlsx).
[11:55] [12:10] Lena Ortiz: i noticed some transcription hiccups in the results — can you confirm what "kv cache warm" means again?
[12:18] Ethan Brooks: kv cache warm just means the model's cached key-value pairs for previous tokens are available; cold starts add a small overhead. Optimize suggests prewarming for high-QPS bursts.
[12:32] [12:50] Maya Chen: ok, wrapping up — recap of commitments and next steps.
[12:55] Maya Chen: we'll run a 2-week pilot scoped to these three endpoints: discharge-summaries, med-history-qna, and appointment-extractions, with hybrid fp8 canary at 10% then ramp to 50% if thresholds hold.
[13:15] Rajiv Nair: success criteria: exact-match drop <=1.0pt absolute, hallucination <1%, and no parser failures in >99.5% of cases. agree?
[13:25] Lena Ortiz: agreed.
[13:28] Markus Vogel: agreed.
[13:30] Maya Chen: i'll send pilot pricing, SOC/ISO package, an SBOM and the exported diffs. ethan will run the kernel bench on your staging infra.
[13:42] Ethan Brooks: noted — i'll reach out to kick off the bench and collect node specs.
[13:50] [14:10] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[14:18] Rajiv Nair: thanks — talk soon.
[14:22] [14:30] End of recording.
